benchmarks.label: Brent

peak.note: Futures intraday wartime high (Wikipedia chronology). Physical Dated Brent (EIA spot via FRED) peaked at $138.21 on 2026-04-07 and was $114.89 on 2026-09-22.

benchmarks.note: Little changed on 2 Oct (-2.4% intraday) after 1 Oct's rise, as markets weighed new US sanctions on Iran's auto and rail sectors and a US-EU dispute over releasing diesel reserves against the continued US-Iran impasse over sanctions relief. Week-ago reuses the prior run's 1 Oct value (1 day earlier, not a full week) — the closest dated figure available.

extra_sources.name: gCaptain (Bloomberg) — JPMorgan and Goldman See Mideast Oil Flows Near Pre-War Levels

benchmarks.label: WTI

peak.note: EIA Cushing spot high via FRED.

benchmarks.note: Fell nearly 4% on 2 Oct as European governments weighed releasing more strategic reserves to ease the diesel squeeze, per Trading Economics commentary; the US separately pressed Germany and France to draw down pledged stocks. Week-ago reuses the prior run's 1 Oct value (1 day earlier, not a full week) — the closest dated figure available.

benchmarks.label: Henry Hub
benchmarks.note: Value is the NYMEX front-month on 2 Oct (Trading Economics), an over one-week low on stronger production and mild-weather demand forecasts; week-ago reuses the prior run's 1 Oct front-month value (1 day earlier, not a full week); pre-crisis is the EIA spot price on 27 Feb (FRED). US LNG feedgas and exports are near records, but the US price is largely insulated.

note: Brent held near $100 and WTI fell on 2 October as the US Treasury sanctioned Iran's carmakers and railways over their use for overland oil, fertiliser and chemical shipments, and Washington pressed Germany and France to release more diesel reserves after both said they'd drawn down little of their pledged stocks; the strait remains formally closed.
